description: Machine-readable provenance for the generated BVH corpus: format shapes, hand-written, committed, runnable with no hardware. Measured fields are produced by libs/motionBvh/tools/check_corpus.py, whose scanner is an independent reading of the format rather than a call into the C++ parser, and are re-checked by motionBvh_corpusManifest. Prose fields are hand-written.
limitations: These are shapes of the format -- hierarchy, channel order, row width, frame time, writer variation -- not any producer's export. No fixture here is named after an application, and none should be: a producer's file in the syntax layer's corpus is where that producer's export becomes the format's definition.
No file here carries a real skeleton, a real unit, or a real basis. Joint names are placeholders and offsets are invented proportions, because this layer refuses to interpret any of them.
Real producer files land with the profiles, under tests/corpus/recorded/, with the redistribution split docs/roadmap/recorded-motion-sources.md §8 describes.

fixtures.pins: CHANNELS declares six and lists three, so the reader runs into the JOINT keyword. Reported as a structural failure naming JOINT -- calling it an unsupported channel would send the reader looking for a channel.

Declares four frames and carries two. There is no frame-count code in the frozen set, so this is VRM_BVH_PARSE_FAILED with the counts in its detail; inventing a code the moment a parser meets this file is the drift the freeze prevents.
A negative frame time. Nothing downstream can place two frames in time with it.
The second of three rows carries five values instead of six. The refusal names that row -- which is the whole reason the motion section is read as lines rather than as a stream of numbers.
Starts at ROOT with no HIERARCHY keyword. The first refusal a file can earn, and it is reported on line 1 rather than after a speculative read.
A joint with CHANNELS and no OFFSET. A joint with no offset is not a bone, and a converter would have to invent one to build a rest pose.
A hierarchy and no MOTION section. The file ends where the animation should start.
A NaN in a motion row. Not a rounding question: a rotation that is not finite has no interpretation at any layer above.
A JOINT block whose brace closes the wrong level, so MOTION arrives where a joint member was expected. Refused where the structure breaks, not at end of file.
A CHANNELS list naming Wrotation. Refused rather than retained as an unknown column: nothing above could attribute its values, and a silently dropped channel shifts every number after it.

A rotation declaration order that is not ZXY, and a joint whose order differs from its parent's. A parser that normalised channels would pass every other fixture and lose this file's only statement about its Euler order.

Two joints with the same name. BVH does not require unique names and real exports repeat them, so a profile matching by name has to be able to see the ambiguity rather than silently take the first match.
A hierarchy with no motion at all: Frames: 0 and no rows. The document is still valid and carries a rest pose.
Everything a writer varies and nothing that changes meaning: lowercase keywords, spaces before the colons, run-together indentation, blank lines between rows, and a trailing blank line.
The smallest thing that is still a BVH file: one ROOT, six channels, an End Site, two rows. Every other fixture is this plus one difference.
Nesting and branching: a three-deep chain beside a second child, so joint order is depth-first declaration order rather than a level walk, and the channel columns follow it.
Position channels on a non-root joint. Real exports carry them for a floating joint, and a parser that assumed six channels mean 'root' would misread the row.
One frame and a zero frame time. A single pose has no interval to describe, so this is a statement rather than an error -- refusing it would refuse the single-pose files real exporters write.
CHANNELS 0 -- a joint the file animates nothing about, which is how a producer exports a static prop beside the rig. What to do about the prop is a profile's decision, one layer up.
